# pantechdynamics_load_balancer (Resource)

Spreads one TCP port across instances. There are two kinds. A vpc_native load balancer (VPC zone, no extra fee) uses one port of a load_balancer public IP and targets instances in one subnet of its network; one public IP can carry several, one per public port, and the subnet's firewall must also allow private_port, with a pantechdynamics_firewall_rule. An appliance load balancer (standard zone) is a managed load balancer VM with its own public address, billed as that VM; it targets instances in its zone, whose security groups must allow private_port. The name, algorithm and targets change in place; changing the kind, zone, public IP, subnet, ports or cidr_list replaces the load balancer.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Spreads HTTP on one public address across two instances in a VPC subnet
# (kind = "vpc_native"). An appliance load balancer for a standard zone follows
# at the end.

resource "pantechdynamics_network" "main" {
  name = "main"
  cidr = "10.0.0.0/16"
}

resource "pantechdynamics_subnet" "web" {
  network_id = pantechdynamics_network.main.id
  name       = "web"
  cidr       = "10.0.1.0/24"
}

# Two targets in the subnet. Use a plan from the "vpc" placement.
resource "pantechdynamics_instance" "web" {
  count      = 2
  name       = "web-${count.index + 1}"
  plan_slug  = "individual"
  image_slug = "ubuntu-24-04"
  subnet_id  = pantechdynamics_subnet.web.id
}

# An address that carries load balancers, one per public port. It is billed as
# a public IP; the load balancer itself has no fee.
resource "pantechdynamics_public_ip" "lb" {
  network_id = pantechdynamics_network.main.id
  purpose    = "load_balancer"
}

# A load balancer opens nothing on its own: the subnet's firewall must allow the
# private port the targets listen on.
resource "pantechdynamics_firewall_rule" "http" {
  subnet_id  = pantechdynamics_subnet.web.id
  number     = 100
  protocol   = "tcp"
  port_start = 8080
  cidr       = "0.0.0.0/0"
}

resource "pantechdynamics_load_balancer" "web" {
  name         = "web"
  public_ip_id = pantechdynamics_public_ip.lb.id
  subnet_id    = pantechdynamics_subnet.web.id
  public_port  = 80
  private_port = 8080        # defaults to public_port
  algorithm    = "leastconn" # roundrobin (default), leastconn or source

  # Targets change in place. The set is the whole list.
  instance_ids = pantechdynamics_instance.web[*].id

  # Only these sources may connect. Omit for any source. Changing it, the
  # ports, the public IP or the subnet replaces the load balancer.
  # cidr_list = ["203.0.113.0/24"]
}

output "web_url" {
  value = "http://${pantechdynamics_load_balancer.web.public_ip_address}"
}

# In a standard zone there is no VPC router: an appliance load balancer is a
# managed load balancer VM with its own public address, billed as that VM. It
# takes zone_id and no public IP or subnet. The targets' security groups must
# allow private_port.
resource "pantechdynamics_instance" "app" {
  count      = 2
  name       = "app-${count.index + 1}"
  plan_slug  = "individual"
  image_slug = "ubuntu-24-04"
  region     = "af-abj"
}

resource "pantechdynamics_load_balancer" "app" {
  name         = "app"
  kind         = "appliance" # inferred from zone_id when left out
  zone_id      = "af-abj-1"
  public_port  = 80
  instance_ids = pantechdynamics_instance.app[*].id
}

output "app_url" {
  value = "http://${pantechdynamics_load_balancer.app.public_ip_address}"
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the load balancer, 1 to 63 characters. Changes in place.
- `public_port` (Number) TCP port clients connect to, 1 to 65535. Only one load balancer per public IP may use a port. Changing it replaces the load balancer.

### Optional

- `algorithm` (String) How connections are spread: "roundrobin" (the default) takes turns, "leastconn" picks the target with the fewest connections, "source" keeps a client on one target. Changes in place.
- `cidr_list` (Set of String) Source addresses allowed to connect, as at most 20 IPv4 CIDRs. Empty (the default) allows any source. Changing it replaces the load balancer.
- `instance_ids` (Set of String) Ids of the instances to spread traffic across, at most 50: for vpc_native each in subnet_id, for an appliance each in zone_id. Empty (the default) means no targets yet. Changes in place: the set is the whole list of targets. An instance cannot be deleted while it is a target.
- `kind` (String) "vpc_native" (a VPC zone: needs public_ip_id and subnet_id) or "appliance" (a standard zone: needs zone_id, and takes no public_ip_id or subnet_id). Left out, it is vpc_native when subnet_id is set and appliance when only zone_id is. Changing it replaces the load balancer.
- `private_port` (Number) Port on each target, 1 to 65535. Defaults to public_port. Changing it replaces the load balancer.
- `public_ip_id` (String) vpc_native only, and required there: id of the public IP clients connect to. It must be active and have purpose load_balancer. Changing it replaces the load balancer.
- `subnet_id` (String) vpc_native only, and required there: id of a subnet in the public IP's network. Every target must be in it. Changing it replaces the load balancer.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))
- `zone_id` (String) Zone of the load balancer, for example "af-abj-1". Required for an appliance. A vpc_native load balancer takes it from subnet_id, so leave it out there. Changing it replaces the load balancer.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the load balancer was created, in RFC 3339 UTC, to the second.
- `id` (String) Identifier of the load balancer, starting with lb_.
- `network_id` (String) Id of the VPC network the load balancer is in. Null for an appliance.
- `observed_state` (String) State of the load balancer as the platform sees it, for example "active".
- `protocol` (String) Protocol balanced. Always "tcp".
- `public_ip_address` (String) The public IPv4 address clients connect to.
- `updated_at` (String) When the load balancer was last changed, in RFC 3339 UTC, to the second.

### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# A load balancer is imported by its id.
terraform import pantechdynamics_load_balancer.web lb_06ggex1abcdefghjkmnpqrstvw
```
